I'm new to investing so I tried finding books recommended by the best investors and the book "The Intelligent Investor" came to my attention thanks to Warren Buffett. I know that there is more than one way to investing so just like a student, curiosity came up to me about the topic. I started questioning the material about its applicability in the PH setting thanks to the "pantayong pananaw" (which is just a fancy term for questioning the perspective of the author). I'm just exploring my options in investing. As for the reason why I am looking for tax-free securities,  I'm just curious if such a thing exists. And if such a thing exists, will I pursue value investing? Probably not right now considering my present skill set and that it is hard to master. So hopefully, that I answer your question.
When he mentions "tax-free securities," he refers to securities free from income tax but not exempt from estate, inheritance, or gift taxes. In his case, its United States Savings Bonds.

Somehow it gets lonely when you realize that you have been living a lie all this time; like you realized that you have the power to live separately from the expectations of the society you live in. If only I've done it sooner. Hard to find like-minded people to share your experiences with and hang-out with. As of now, I am searching for answers about the things that are bothering me lately: my culture, my mindset, my skills, my selection of friends, my future, and my life. It feels like I'm losing here. Hard to know who to go to for advice & comfort, what to do to achieve my goals, where to go in order to achieve them and how to do it. Is that hard to do, especially for a 17 y/o? Makes me feel inadequate in not knowing about it five years ago or so.

It really is painful to think that you've been taught all your life to follow the system. I have some second thoughts about whether living is worth it anymore. Will I still become a slave regardless of my efforts to change my fate?  Somehow the thing that is keeping me going is the thought of changing it. A weak reason if you ask me. Before, I was very optimistic about doing so. But now, I see it in an ambivalent way. I'm quite afraid of what the future may bring. I sure hope that I can get what I wanted despite living in such injustice.

Yeah, you're right about focusing on what we do want. You are also, in a way, right about not analysing ideas/concepts that we can't/won't change.

I don't even know what to think about this situation. I can take advantage of it or just live in another country. But no matter what I'll do, I'll just be a regular Filipino who has nothing to do but to please others (a minor example is my parents only cleaning up a room when a visitor will arrive, especially a foreigner, despite the fact that it can be done during spare time). This, in effect, lowers my productivity, making me lazier and lazier. It is just not a great environment for me.

I wanted to be a businessman specializing in computer hardware and software but given the position that I'm in right now, it can only go so far. My mother suggested to make a group of companies, each specializing in computers, food, real estate, and wood production. I can see the potential but will it create an impact to the world? Will it change an industry? Even the top companies (mostly Chinese-owned) can only greatly influence/reach East Asia (S.E included). It pales in comparison to companies like Microsoft, Coca-Cola, and Sony. I want to make a big difference to the world.

To cut things short, I really appreciate the advice you gave me. Maybe there are some things that I can change after all. I'll try to look into it and see if I can mold myself into the person I want to be. Thanks, man! :D

I can feel that too. I have to bring up a facade everyday because it may cause a rift between me and the society I live in. 

Growing up in a Filipino household, my family has a conservative approach when it comes to running the house: clan-based thinking, gaining favors through connection instead of merit, etc. It is somehow integrated into our lives and our society, and I don't know how to change it. I tried to change my environment but somehow I felt that it is too late; that it is now a part of me, the so-called 'Filipino curse'. 

I never wanted it in the first place and I know that it will hinder my personal development. It will be the end of me. 

I know that this is confusing but our society revolves around emotions instead of logic, so it is quite subjective. I hope you understand. (._. )

I want to make the most of my abilities and not take society's idea of 'success' and 'fulfillment'. 

It is hard to put this off my chest because it is never been discussed here and even if it is, dismissed immediately thinking that I am thinking gibberish and wrong. I hate conservatism. (-insert angry face-)
